values.note: Forest Service dispersed camping: no reservations. 'Dispersed camping in one location is allowable up to 14 days in any 30-day period.' Not allowed near developed sites (campgrounds, picnic areas, trailheads); keep the campsite within 150 ft of the road.

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/camping-cabins ('Recreationist can camp anywhere in the National Forest outside a designated campground'; 'Dispersed camping in one location is allowable up to 14 days in any 30-day period'; 'Keep your campsite within 150 feet from a roadway'), read 2026-10-21

summary: Confirmed from the GW&J forest's dispersed-camping rules: first-come, no reservations (as recorded), plus a 14-days-in-30 limit; VA DWR's Flagpole Knob page confirms the note's road description. Hookups/facilities (The Dyrt, reported) and free fees left as recorded. Not stated by any agency page: the site itself, season, facilities. Note: dropped 'No water, toilets' (in hookups/facilities).
flags: Access criteria (AWH 2026-10-21 4WD rule, human decides): Virginia DWR's own Flagpole Knob page (https://dwr.virginia.gov/vbwt/sites/flagpole-knob/, read 2026-10-21) says 'Forest Service Road 85 towards the Flagpole Knob summit is remote, narrow, very steep, deeply rutted, and rocky. Only experienced overlanding/off-roading drivers should attempt this road.' It does not say '4WD' in words, but it is an agency statement that the access road is for off-road vehicles/drivers; EKKO is not 4WD. The Forest Service pages name no road condition.
note: High-elevation campsite just west of Flagpole Knob.  Access road may not suitable for vehicles with low ground clearance.  --AWH  Just below the Flagpole Knob summit (4,398 ft). The Dyrt lists about 5 free dispersed sites around the summit (8 reviews 2020-25, nearly all 5*). Sunrise and sunset views are the draw, but this is the exposed end: reviewers say to use the tree-covered sites below the top on windy nights. Raccoons carry off shoes and trash left out. Busy on spring weekends, often empty otherwise. The approach is 3.6 mi of rutted, rocky FR 85A from Briery Branch Gap (VA DWR: experienced off-road drivers only) or the longer, easier Switzer Lake/Union Springs route from US 33. A Subaru Outback (2022) and an AWD VW Tiguan made it; a ProMaster campervan did in 2024 and its driver advised against it; others say 4x4 required. No tables. Some AT&T and Verizon signal, none on T-Mobile. --Claude
